title: The compose failure-lesson channel stores build boilerplate instead of the diagnostic, so the drafter's only runtime tea
description:
The compose failure-lesson channel stores build boilerplate instead of the diagnostic, so the drafter's only runtime teaching channel carries no information about why a verify failed.

MEASURED 2026-09-08. On gaps whose lessons were recorded after 20:30, every verify_failed lesson's `reason` field is exactly 200 characters and every one of them is consumed by the build preamble:
  "== install == == resolve == DRYRUN_EXIT=0  @types/bun@1.3.14  typescript@5.9.3  bun-types@1.3.14 ... [3.00ms] done == typecheck == $ tsc --noEmit src/resolvers/sub"
The string ends mid-path, exactly where the TypeScript error would begin. The accompanying `raw_excerpt` fields measured 479 and 529 characters, also ending mid-error.

WHY THIS MATTERS. feature-compose.ts:2213-2214 renders `raw_excerpt` back to the drafter on a later attempt ("raw verify output (verbatim, from the prior failed attempt)"), and the code's own comment at 6190-6194 states that this is "the one learning loop that actually works" and that feeding it a misleading label "is a law-8 failure (the load-bearing fact is available but wrong at the moment of use) on the only channel with a runtime reader". The same law-8 failure is happening one level down: the label may now be right, but the evidence attached to it is the package list.

WHY IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS SLICE. At feature-compose.ts:3081 the lesson is written as `reason: reason.slice(0, 200), raw_excerpt: reason.slice(0, 1500)`. The 1500-char excerpt would be ample, but the stored excerpts are only ~500 chars, so `failedVerify.output` has ALREADY been truncated before it reaches this line. lessonReason is assembled at 6199-6204 as `failedApply?.detail ?? failedVerify?.output ?? semantic_gate?.reason ?? verdict`, so the cap is upstream of that, in whatever captures verify output. Note this is not a universal cap: a compose report inspected earlier the same day carried a 336KB verify output, so short outputs are a property of this path rather than of verification generally.

TWO INDEPENDENT FIXES, EITHER OF WHICH HELPS.
(a) Preserve the error, not the head. The classifier at feature-compose.ts:3063-3067 already greps `bad.output` for TS1128/TS1005/TS1109/TS1110 and TS2304/TS2552/TS2554/TS2551/TS2345/TS2322, so the error-bearing lines are identifiable at that point. Build the lesson `reason` from the lines matching /error TS\d+|\d+ fail|FAIL|Error:/ rather than from the first 200 characters. A head-slice of a build log is almost never the diagnostic, because build logs put the environment first and the failure last.
(b) Find and raise the upstream truncation so `failedVerify.output` still contains the error by the time the lesson is written.

WHY NOW. verify_failed is the dominant failure class on the gaps that currently localise successfully: among failure lessons recorded on region-armed gaps after 20:30, verify_failed is 57.1% versus a 15.7% historic base rate (n=7, P(>=4)=0.014 against that base). As localisation improves, the next bottleneck is the drafter learning why its applied change failed its tests, and that is exactly the information this channel is currently discarding.

FALSIFIER. Read any verify_failed lesson recorded after this change and confirm its reason or raw_excerpt contains a line matching /error TS\d+/ or a test-failure summary rather than the install/resolve preamble.
